measures.id: City of Raleigh Housing Bonds Referendum
measures.title: City of Raleigh Housing Bonds
measures.summary: Asks whether the City of Raleigh may borrow up to $101,500,000 by issuing bonds for community development programs that build or rehabilitate multifamily and single-family housing inside the city, principally for people with low and moderate incomes, including loans and other financial help and related land acquisition. The official ballot statement estimates the total cost over the life of the bonds at $167,885,618 ($101,500,000 principal plus $66,385,618 interest) and estimates the property tax increase needed to repay them at $0 per year per $100,000 of property value. If approved, the city may levy additional property taxes in an amount sufficient to pay the principal and interest.
measures.yesMeans: The City of Raleigh may issue up to $101,500,000 in bonds for housing programs principally for people with low and moderate incomes, and may levy property taxes sufficient to repay them.
measures.noMeans: The City of Raleigh may not issue these $101,500,000 in housing bonds.

measures.id: City of Raleigh Transportation Bonds Referendum
measures.title: City of Raleigh Transportation Bonds
measures.summary: Asks whether the City of Raleigh may borrow up to $101,500,000 by issuing bonds for transportation improvements inside and outside the city limits, including streets, sidewalks and streetscapes, bridges, bicycle lanes, curbs and drains, traffic controls, greenways, bus and train station and shelter improvements, and related land. The official ballot statement estimates the total cost over the life of the bonds at $164,607,118 ($101,500,000 principal plus $63,107,118 interest) and estimates the property tax increase needed to repay them at $0 per year per $100,000 of property value. If approved, the city may levy additional property taxes in an amount sufficient to pay the principal and interest.
measures.yesMeans: The City of Raleigh may issue up to $101,500,000 in bonds for street, sidewalk, bridge, bicycle lane, greenway, transit stop and related transportation improvements, and may levy property taxes sufficient to repay them.
measures.noMeans: The City of Raleigh may not issue these $101,500,000 in transportation bonds.
